It urges DOJ to restore and expand BJA, COVID‑19 Hate Crimes Act, and Jabara‑Heyer NO HATE Act programs and to support community services, online‑hate responses, and AANHPI education.

119/hres/1116.title: Commemorating the 5-year remembrance of the March 16, 2021, shootings in the Atlanta, Georgia, region and denouncing continuing anti-Asian hate, including the resurgence of xenophobic and anti-immigrant rhetoric.

description.summary: This bill bans selling optional vehicle safety features only as bundles with non‑safety options, requiring they be available for separate purchase or included as standard trim with separate price disclosure. It applies to manufacturers and first purchasers under 49 U.S.C. 30102, defines covered ADAS and alert features, and gives FTC and state enforcement.

impact.summary: The bill requires automakers, dealers, and lessors to sell optional safety features like automatic emergency braking, lane keeping, and driver monitoring separately from luxury packages or include them as standard. The Federal Trade Commission enforces it and state attorneys general may sue for penalties.

119/hr/7372.title: Safety is Not For Sale Act

description.summary: The bill requires DOT to amend the automatic emergency braking standard so AEB systems detect and respond to pedestrians, bicyclists, motorcyclists and other vulnerable road users in daylight and low light across skin, clothing, and gear. It applies to passenger motor vehicles made for sale in the United States.

impact.summary: The bill requires the Secretary of Transportation (NHTSA) to amend the Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard for automatic emergency braking so AEB on passenger motor vehicles operates in daylight and low light and detects pedestrians, bicyclists, motorcyclists, wheelchair users, and ATV/tractor riders. It affects automakers.

119/hr/7353.title: Magnus White and Safe Streets for Everyone Act of 2026

description.summary: The SAFE Exit Act directs the Secretary of Transportation to amend FMVSS No. 206 within two years to require power‑independent, easy‑to‑find manual door releases that mechanically disengage electronic latches and labeled performance and emergency‑responder access provisions when vehicle electrical power is lost. It covers new vehicles with electronic door latches.

impact.summary: Mandates DOT (Secretary/NHTSA) to amend FMVSS No.206 within two years to require intuitive, power‑independent manual door releases and emergency responder access when vehicle electrical power is lost. U.S. automakers and motor‑vehicle manufacturers must install these devices on new vehicles and comply with DOT/NHTSA rules.

description.summary: The bill exempts Purple Heart and Medal of Honor recipients from certain passport fees by amending the Passport Act of 1920. It requires the State Department's Consular Affairs office to make a memorandum of understanding with the Defense Department to verify awards and set documentation for eligible applications and renewals.

impact.summary: The bill exempts Purple Heart and Medal of Honor recipients from certain passport fees. It directs the Secretary of State, via the Assistant Secretary for Consular Affairs, to enter an MOU with the Secretary of Defense and DoD to verify service records and set documentation.

119/hr/7398.title: Passports for Purple Hearts and Medals of Honor Act

description.summary: The bill bars the SEC and exchanges from prohibiting or conditioning closed-end funds' investments in private funds or limiting listing or sales because of such investments. It defines private fund by reference to the Investment Advisers Act, covers closed-end companies including BDCs, and preserves fiduciary, valuation, liquidity, and redemption obligations.

impact.summary: The bill bars the SEC from forbidding closed-end investment companies, including business development companies, to invest any or all assets in private funds as defined by the Investment Advisers Act. It prevents national securities exchanges from refusing to list or trade those closed-end company securities.

description.summary: The ACCESS Act of 2026 raises the crowdfunding threshold requiring financial statements reviewed by an independent accountant from $100,000 to $250,000 and lets the SEC raise it to $400,000 on recommendation of the small-business and investor advocates. It covers issuers using the Regulation Crowdfunding exemption and corrects section 4(a)(6) cross-references.

impact.summary: The bill raises the crowdfunding threshold requiring an independent public-accountant review from $100,000 to $250,000 for issuers using Section 4A. It lets the SEC, after recommendations by the Office of the Advocate for Small Business Capital Formation and the Investor Advocate, raise it to $400,000.

description.summary: This resolution impeaches DHS Secretary Kristi Lynn Arnold Noem, alleging obstruction of Congress and breach of public trust for denying Member oversight, withholding FEMA funds, and directing ICE warrantless arrests and raids. If adopted it would formally impeach Noem and send articles to the Senate, targeting her DHS conduct.

impact.summary: The resolution impeaches Kristi Lynn Arnold Noem, Secretary of Homeland Security. It says she blocked oversight of DHS and ICE detention sites, oversaw ICE warrantless arrests and Chicago raids, and directed FEMA to withhold Emergency Food and Shelter and Shelter and Services Program funds.

119/hres/996.title: Impeaching Kristi Lynn Arnold Noem, Secretary of Homeland Security, for high crimes and misdemeanors.

description.summary: The House resolution urges the Secretary of Defense to review 10 U.S.C. §504 to determine whether to authorize enlistment under subsection (b)(2) for aliens holding DACA employment authorization documents. It would cover DACA recipients with DHS-issued work permits seeking to enlist in the U.S. Armed Forces under that enlistment authority.

impact.summary: This resolution urges the Secretary of Defense to review 10 U.S.C. §504 for authorizing enlistment of aliens with DHS DACA EADs. The review would involve the Department of Defense and could affect DACA recipients seeking to join the U.S. Armed Forces.

119/hres/994.title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that the Secretary of Defense should review section 504 of title 10, United States Code, for purposes related to enlisting certain aliens in the Armed Forces.

description.summary: The bill amends the ACA to impose civil penalties ($10k–$50k negligent; up to $200k knowing) and criminal penalties (up to 10 years) on agents and brokers who submit false enrollment information. Federal Exchanges must verify agent-assisted enrollments, document consent, delay commissions until inconsistencies resolve, and regulate marketing organizations.

impact.summary: The bill lets HHS require verification of agent or broker enrollments in Exchange plans and imposes civil and criminal penalties on agents, brokers, and marketing organizations. It affects HHS Exchanges, issuers, agents, and consumers by requiring documentation, delaying commissions, reporting issuer terminations, preventing unauthorized disenrollments.

description.summary: The Stop CMV Act authorizes hospitals and health care entities to screen newborns up to 21 days old for congenital cytomegalovirus and requires state screening standards. It authorizes HRSA and CDC grants, expands NIH research, and tasks the Advisory Committee and state health officers with procedures, reporting, training, and follow‑up.

impact.summary: The Stop CMV Act would let hospitals and other health care entities screen every infant 21 days or younger for congenital cytomegalovirus and require State health officials to adopt approved screening and reporting procedures. HRSA, CDC, NIH would fund grants, data systems, education, research.

description.summary: The Rural Obstetrics Readiness Act establishes HRSA grant programs and a teleconsultation pilot to support obstetric emergency training, equipment, workforce development, transfer protocols, and rapid telehealth consultation. Awards go to rural hospitals, critical access and rural emergency hospitals, consortia, States and Tribes, and facilities lacking obstetric units; it authorizes $5M (2026–2028) and $15M (2026–2029).

impact.summary: The bill requires HHS/HRSA to grant funds for obstetric emergency training, equipment, staffing, and transfer protocols to rural hospitals, critical access hospitals, rural emergency hospitals, and consortia in maternity shortage areas. It also creates an HRSA teleconsultation pilot for States, political subdivisions, and Indian Tribes.

description.summary: The bill requires group health plans and issuers to cover PSA screening without cost‑sharing for high‑risk men 40+. High‑risk includes African‑American men and men with a first‑degree family history or relevant genetic alteration, effective for plan years beginning January 1, 2025.

impact.summary: The bill requires group health plans and insurers to cover PSA screening without cost-sharing for men 40+ at high risk. It affects private insurers, employer-sponsored and self-insured group plans, the USPSTF guidance, and high-risk groups such as African American men and men with family history.

description.summary: The Act funds DOL competitive grants to community colleges, career and technical education centers, and industry partnerships to build immersive technology career pathways using VR/AR/MR for workforce training. Grants run up to five years, prioritize employer-aligned and accessible programs, and require reporting, independent evaluation, and publication of best practices.

impact.summary: The bill tells the Secretary of Labor to fund community colleges, area CTE schools, Tribal colleges, and industry partnerships to build immersive (VR/AR/XR/MR) career-pathway training. Grants prioritize employer-aligned programs serving veterans and people with disabilities, last up to five years, and require DOL reporting.

119/s/2855.title: Immersive Technology for the American Workforce Act of 2025

description.summary: This House resolution designates March as "Multiple System Atrophy Awareness Month" and expresses support for increased public awareness and funding for research toward therapeutics. It concerns a rare, often fatal neurodegenerative disorder affecting tens of thousands in the United States and represents the House's nonbinding endorsement of awareness and research.

impact.summary: This House resolution designates March as "Multiple System Atrophy Awareness Month" and supports research funding for MSA. It signals support for about 25,000–75,000 U.S. patients, their families, researchers and centers like Stanford's MSA Center of Excellence and agencies such as NIH/NINDS.

119/hres/1117.title: Expressing support for the designation of March as "Multiple System Atrophy Awareness Month" to strengthen public awareness of this neurodegenerative disorder.

description.summary: The resolution requests the Secretary of State to submit, within 30 days under section 502B(c), a State Department statement prepared with DRL and the Office of the Legal Adviser on Cameroon's human rights practices. It requires details on violations, treatment of non‑Cameroonians sent to Cameroon, U.S. assurances, and 2025–26 transfers.

impact.summary: Senate requests a 502B(c) report from the Secretary of State on Cameroon's human rights for congressional committees. Prepared with the Assistant Secretary for DRL and State Legal Adviser, it must cover Cameroon government abuses, U.S. removals including 2025–2026 cases, and risks from U.S. security assistance.

119/sres/637.title: A resolution requesting information on the Republic of Cameroon's human rights practices pursuant to section 502B(c) of the Foreign Assistance Act 1961.

description.summary: The POINT Act criminalizes executive "election interference" and forbids using government property, personnel, information systems, or funds to influence, delay, or alter elections. It applies to the President, Vice President, EOP and senior agency officials including AG, FBI and DNI directors and cabinet managers, forbids military or federal deployments except under the Voting Rights Act or for secession/rebellion.

impact.summary: The POINT Act criminalizes federal executive election interference by named officials—President, Vice President, Attorney General, FBI and DNI directors, and cabinet managers—using government property, personnel, systems, or funds. It forbids Armed Forces deployment to affect State elections, lets States sue, and preserves Voting Rights exceptions.

description.summary: The bill requires DHS to verify personal and biometric data and conduct in-person vetting of Afghan evacuees, maintain a vetting database, report quarterly, and permit GAO audits. It applies to noncitizen, non-military evacuees from Afghanistan during the 2021 U.S. evacuation operations and bars unvetted individuals from Federal means-tested benefits, unemployment.

impact.summary: The bill directs DHS to verify personal and biometric data, conduct in‑person vetting, and create a database for non‑citizens evacuated from Afghanistan, including Operation Allies Welcome evacuees, and report to Congress. Evacuees who refuse vetting are barred from unemployment compensation and Federal means‑tested public benefits.

119/hr/7759.title: Afghanistan Vetting and Accountability Act of 2026

description.summary: Reauthorizes USDA’s heirs property relending program to 2031 and funds nonprofit legal and accounting cooperative agreements to resolve ownership and succession of multi‑owner farmland or forestland. Provides $60 million per year for FY2027–2031 (≤3% admin), prioritizes underserved heirs (limited‑resource, socially disadvantaged, veterans), and requires annual public reports to Congress.

impact.summary: The bill reauthorizes heirs property relending and farmland data programs through 2031 and authorizes $60 million annually for USDA cooperative agreements funding nonprofit legal services. It affects underserved heirs with undivided farmland or forest interests, nonprofit legal providers, and USDA programs requiring ownership to enroll.

119/hr/7761.title: Heirs Education and Investment to Resolve Succession of Property Act

description.summary: The Quantum in Practice Act amends the National Quantum Initiative Act to add "modeling, simulation" to the definition of quantum information science and to insert "quantum molecular modeling or simulation" among section 401(b)(3) research priorities. It applies to federal programs implementing the NQI Act.

impact.summary: The bill amends the National Quantum Initiative Act to add modeling and simulation and to include quantum molecular modeling or simulation in the QIS research program. It would guide NSF, NIST, DOE labs, universities, and researchers to research chemical, pharmaceutical, battery, fertilizer, and defense industries.

description.summary: The Kelsey Smith Act requires providers and carriers to promptly disclose available device location data to law enforcement or PSAPs in emergencies. Requests must assert recent 911 contact or reasonable suspicion of imminent danger, include subscriber or next‑of‑kin consent or documented efforts, and be recorded by the agency.

impact.summary: The bill amends 18 U.S.C. 2703 to require providers to promptly give device location to law enforcement or public safety answering points (911 centers) in emergencies. It affects wireless carriers, ISPs, investigative agencies, subscribers and next-of-kin consent procedures, and intersects state disclosure laws.

description.summary: The bill amends the Sherman Act to deem purchases of residential real estate by certain large investors civil Section 1 antitrust violations. It covers REITs, insurers, and investment companies or private funds with ≥$150,000,000 AUM buying single‑family homes, condos, townhouses, or zoned land, with a homebuilder exception and 90‑day delay.

impact.summary: The bill bars purchases of single-family homes, condos, townhouses, or zoned land by covered entities: REITs, insurance companies, and investment companies or private funds with at least $150,000,000 assets under management. DOJ Antitrust Division must prioritize review and enforcement; effective 90 days after enactment.

description.summary: The bill amends Exchange Act §15B to set MSRB membership: a 15‑member (odd‑number) board with a regulated‑representative majority and minimum broker‑dealer, bank, advisor, and public seats. Those rules govern MSRB appointments, terms, interim members, and SEC removal authority, affecting regulation of brokers, dealers, municipal advisors, municipal entities, and investors.

impact.summary: The bill would amend Section 15B to set MSRB membership rules, 15 members, regulated/public quotas, staggered three‑year terms, and SEC appointment and removal authority. It would affect the MSRB, the SEC, municipal securities brokers and dealers (including bank dealers), municipal advisors, issuers/obligated persons, and investors.

119/s/3935.title: Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board Reform Act of 2026

description.summary: The bill criminalizes knowingly transporting a minor across state or foreign lines to obtain puberty blockers, cross‑sex hormones, or gender‑altering surgery, punishable by up to 10 years' imprisonment and civil suits. It also denies federal funds to governments that permit, facilitate, or fail to cooperate with investigations of such transport.

impact.summary: The bill criminalizes knowingly transporting a minor across state lines to obtain puberty blockers, cross‑sex hormones, or surgical sex‑change procedures, affecting parents and medical providers. It also bars federal funds to states or localities that allow such transport or refuse to cooperate with DOJ investigations.

119/hr/7420.title: Stop Gender Trafficking of Minors Act

description.summary: The Clean Competition Act adds a carbon intensity charge to the tax code that levies fees based on facility or national‑industry carbon intensity and requires annual facility reporting of emissions, electricity sourcing, and production quantities. It covers covered entities, eligible facilities, and covered primary goods within defined covered national industries.

impact.summary: The Clean Competition Act creates a carbon‑intensity charge requiring covered entities and eligible facilities to report GHG emissions, electricity use, and output to the Secretary (Treasury), the Administrator (EPA), and the Secretary of Energy. It sets carbon‑intensity formulas affecting U.S. energy‑intensive manufacturers and import classifications.

description.summary: Creates a carbon‑intensity charge in the tax code that taxes emissions per unit by requiring facilities to report GHG emissions, electricity use, and production. Applies to eligible facilities producing covered primary goods and assigns Treasury, EPA, and Energy to calculate intensities, handle petitions, and administer charges, rebates, and carbon clubs.

impact.summary: The Clean Competition Act adds a carbon‑intensity charge and carbon border adjustment to the Internal Revenue Code. It makes U.S. manufacturers (covered entities) of goods like steel, cement, aluminum, and chemicals report emissions and energy data to Treasury, EPA (GHGRP), and Energy for billing.

description.summary: Creates 49 U.S.C. §5308 authorizing formula grants for urban transit operating, planning, security, and safety projects, with operating grants at 80% federal share. Apportionments use reported operating expenses; recipients must maintain non‑Federal spending, cannot convert fixed‑route to third‑party on‑demand, and may reallocate up to 10% of section 5336 funds.

impact.summary: The bill creates §5308 authorizing FTA grants to urbanized areas for transit operating, planning, security, and safety. It sets an 80% federal share for operating aid and requires transit recipients (for example, New York MTA) to certify they will maintain non‑Federal operating and security spending.

description.summary: The bill requires DHS to verify identities and biometrics and to conduct in-person interviews of noncitizens evacuated from Afghanistan between Jan 20, 2021 and Jan 20, 2022. Unvetted evacuees are barred from unemployment and all means-tested federal benefits until vetted, and DHS must provide quarterly reports while GAO audits compliance.

impact.summary: DHS must verify personal and biometric data, conduct in person vetting, and list criminal and benefit records for non United States citizens evacuated from Afghanistan. Noncompliant evacuees would be ineligible for unemployment compensation and Federal means tested programs such as SNAP, Medicaid, and TANF.

119/s/3310.title: Afghanistan Vetting and Accountability Act of 2025

description.summary: The bill creates a tiered Public Service Loan Forgiveness for Federal Direct Loans made after enactment, forgiving 15% increments and full balance after 120 qualifying payments. It covers borrowers employed in certified public service jobs, requires employment certification (including self‑certification), cancels interest on forgiven amounts, and auto‑defers loans during processing.

impact.summary: Bill requires Department of Education to cancel parts of Federal Direct Loans for borrowers in qualifying public service jobs (government and qualifying nonprofits). It cancels 15% after each 24 payments through 96, forgives remaining balance after 120, requires ED certification, cancels interest, and defers loans.

119/hr/6284.title: Strengthening Loan Forgiveness for Public Service Workers Act

description.summary: S.2957 raises the portion of urbanized-area formula grants reserved for small transit‑intensive cities under 49 U.S.C. 5336(h)(3) from 3 percent to 5 percent. It changes allocations for Federal Transit Administration urbanized-area formula funds, increasing federal shares available to qualifying small cities and their transit agencies.

impact.summary: The bill changes 49 U.S.C. §5336(h)(3) to raise the set‑aside for small transit intensive cities from 3% to 5% of formula grants. That change would shift FTA allocations toward local transit agencies in qualifying small urbanized areas and state transportation agencies that receive them.

description.summary: The resolution impeaches Attorney General Pamela Bondi for obstruction, EFTA violations, and abuse of DOJ power, submitting articles for Senate trial and removal. It targets Bondi's official conduct over DOJ/FBI Epstein files, redactions, and prosecutorial or personnel actions.

impact.summary: The House resolution impeaches Attorney General Pamela Bondi for obstructing Congress, flouting the Epstein Files Transparency Act, and abusing Department of Justice and FBI prosecutorial and investigatory powers. It would affect Bondi, the Department of Justice (including the FBI), the House Oversight Committee, Epstein survivors, and Donald J. Trump.

119/hres/1119.title: Impeaching Pamela Bondi, Attorney General of the United States, for high crimes and misdemeanors.

description.summary: This Senate resolution honors Reverend Jesse L. Jackson, Sr., commends his civil‑rights and human‑rights leadership, and extends condolences to his family. It requests the Secretary of the Senate transmit an enrolled copy to his family and is an expression of recognition, not a law.

impact.summary: The Senate resolution honors Reverend Jesse L. Jackson Sr.'s leadership, citing Operation PUSH, National Rainbow Coalition, his presidential campaigns, and service as a special envoy to Africa. It extends condolences and requests the Secretary of the Senate transmit an enrolled copy to Reverend Jackson's family.

119/sres/629.title: A resolution honoring the life and legacy of Reverend Jesse Louis Jackson, Sr., and commending him for his significant leadership during the Civil Rights Movement and his decades of advocacy in pursuit of justice, equality, and human rights.

description.summary: The bill lets Indian Tribes run Federal meat inspections under self‑determination contracts with USDA standards, oversight, enforcement, and FTCA protection. It covers mobile or stationary processors at least 51% tribe‑owned, permits federally inspected labeling and interstate shipment, and requires insurance and annual certifications.

impact.summary: The bill lets Indian Tribes and Tribal organizations conduct USDA/FSIS meat inspections at tribally owned mobile or stationary processors (51%+ ownership). It makes tribal inspectors subject to FTCA, preserves USDA oversight and labeling for interstate meat, and affects processors of beef, bison, reindeer and insurers.

119/s/3994.title: PRIME Meat Processing in Indian Country Act

description.summary: Creates a five‑year USDA pilot paying producers when national seasonal prices for certain produce fall below a five‑year reference because of imports. Applies to asparagus, bell peppers, blueberries, cucumbers, squash sold raw in a four‑week window; limits recipients to producers with average AGI <$5,000,000 and ≥75% farming income; authorizes $200M/year.

impact.summary: The Protecting Our Produce Act would require USDA to run a pilot paying U.S. asparagus, bell pepper, blueberry, cucumber, and squash producers when import-driven seasonal prices fall below a five-year reference price. Payments are authorized at $200,000,000 annually and target producers with under $5,000,000 AGI.

description.summary: The bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow charitable rollovers from individual retirement accounts to donor-advised funds by removing the exclusion of funds described in section 4966(d)(2). It applies to IRA distributions after enactment and affects IRA owners and donor-advised funds covered by section 4966(d)(2).

impact.summary: The bill would let people transfer IRA distributions directly into donor advised funds. It affects IRA owners, account custodians (banks and brokerages), donor advised fund sponsors (community foundations, Fidelity Charitable), public charities, and the IRS.

119/s/3975.title: IRA Charitable Rollover Facilitation and Enhancement Act of 2026

description.summary: The bill requires the Secretary of the Interior to restore within 15 days any interpretive or educational exhibit, sign, plaque, or display removed from public view at Independence National Historical Park after January 21, 2026, to its appearance on that date. It prohibits altering such exhibits without express congressional authorization.

impact.summary: The bill directs the Secretary of the Interior and the National Park Service to restore exhibits, signs, and plaques at Independence National Historical Park in Philadelphia removed after January 21, 2026. It also bars any future alteration without express authorization from Congress.

description.summary: The bill directs the Comptroller General to, within one year, study options to remove housing barriers and improve housing for elderly and disabled people, including analyzing impacts of providing capital advances to Section 202 and Section 811 supportive‑housing programs. It covers elderly and disabled persons and Sections 202 and 811.

impact.summary: The bill directs the Comptroller General to study, within one year, how to remove barriers and improve housing for elderly and disabled. It must examine impacts of providing capital advances for HUD's Section 202 (elderly) and Section 811 (disability) programs, affecting HUD, developers, tenants.

description.summary: The bill exempts assistance under sections 501, 502, 504, 515, 533, and 538 of the Housing Act from NEPA's "major Federal action" requirement for construction/modification of housing on qualifying infill sites. It excludes greenfields, road-only sites, and FEMA very/high-risk tracts, and requires USDA to report to Congress within five years.

impact.summary: Law exempts USDA Rural Development housing assistance (sections 501, 502, 504, 515, 533, 538) from NEPA for residential projects on qualifying infill sites. It affects rural borrowers and developers using USDA Rural Housing programs, excludes FEMA high‑risk tracts, and requires a five‑year USDA report.

description.summary: The bill reauthorizes and updates the National Domestic Preparedness Consortium, adds the Rural Domestic Preparedness Consortium and MxV Learning Institute, and renames certain member entries. It authorizes $111M–$125M for FY2027–2031, expands training to state, tribal, territorial and public‑safety partners, and preserves FY2023 minimum allocations with proportional distribution.

impact.summary: The bill reauthorizes the National Domestic Preparedness Consortium and adds the Academy of Counter‑Terrorist Education and Rural Domestic Preparedness Consortium. It authorizes FY2027–2031 consortium funding ($111M, $114M, $117M, $120M, $125M) and directs the Secretary of Homeland Security to preserve FY2023 funding or proportionally allocate cuts.

119/s/3973.title: National Domestic Preparedness Consortium Reauthorization Act

description.summary: The Stop Post-Disaster Vultures Act prohibits institutional investors from soliciting offers to buy properties in a declared major disaster area for six months after the declaration. It defines such investors as those owning 75 or more single‑family homes and applies to offers for lots, parcels, or homes in affected areas.

impact.summary: The bill amends the Stafford Act to bar institutional investors—defined as any individual or entity owning 75 or more single‑family homes—from making offers to buy lots, parcels, or homes within a FEMA-declared major disaster area for six months after the declaration. It targets REITs and private equity.

description.summary: This bill bars states from imposing retroactive taxes on the value of assets owned by individuals who were nonresidents when the taxing law is enacted. It covers taxes attributable to any period before the law's enactment and takes effect January 1, 2026.

impact.summary: The Keep Jobs in California Act of 2026 bars States from levying retroactive taxes on nonresident individuals' assets when the tax uses asset values dated before the law's enactment. It would affect the California Franchise Tax Board, ex-California residents, and banks.

119/hr/7619.title: Keep Jobs in California Act of 2026

description.summary: The bill directs the Comptroller General to complete within one year a study identifying options to remove barriers and improve housing for elderly and disabled people. It requires assessing impacts of capital advances for HUD Section 202 (elderly) and Section 811 (disabled) supportive housing.

impact.summary: The bill requires the Comptroller General to study, within one year, options to remove barriers and improve housing for elderly and disabled persons. It must analyze potential impacts of providing capital advances for HUD's Section 202 and Section 811 supportive housing programs.

description.summary: This resolution designates April 5, 2026, as "Barth Syndrome Awareness Day" and urges awareness, earlier diagnosis, research, treatment development, and regulatory pathways for Barth syndrome. It covers Barth syndrome—a rare, primarily male genetic disorder caused by TAFAZZIN mutations—and concerns patients, clinicians, researchers, clinics, and advocacy groups in the United States.

impact.summary: H. Res. 1060 designates April 5, 2026, as "Barth Syndrome Awareness Day" and expresses House support for awareness, diagnosis, research, and treatment development. It highlights patients and families, the Barth Syndrome Foundation, the Kennedy Krieger Institute Barth Syndrome Clinic, researchers, and the FDA's patient‑focused program.

119/hres/1060.title: Expressing support for the designation of April 5, 2026, as "Barth Syndrome Awareness Day".

description.summary: The bill directs the Congressional Budget Office with the Council of Economic Advisers to publish within 180 days a study on the long-term economic impact of immigration policies beginning January 20, 2025. It studies 20–40 year effects on industries, demographics, safety, innovation, businesses, revenues, and requires DHS, BLS, IRS data.

impact.summary: The bill directs the Congressional Budget Office with the Council of Economic Advisers to study immigration policies beginning January 20, 2025 over twenty to forty years. It requires DHS, BLS, IRS to share data and assess impacts on workers, small businesses, GDP, migration, tax revenues.

119/hr/7345.title: Studying Disastrous Impacts of Mass Deportation Act

description.summary: The Carbon Resource Innovation Act amends IRC section 45Q to make solid and liquid carbon capture facilities eligible for the sequestration tax credit. It defines such facilities, requires capture measurement and verification at disposal, injection, or utilization, sets a 1,000‑ton threshold, and permits underground storage if carbon does not escape.

impact.summary: Expands Section 45Q tax credit to cover solid or liquid carbon capture facilities, requires measurement/verification at capture and disposal/injection/utilization, and permits underground storage under Treasury/IRS rules. It would affect power plants, steel and cement manufacturers, carbon-capture firms, taxpayers, and the Treasury and IRS.

description.summary: The bill requires the Secretary of State, in each U.S.-Hong Kong Policy Act certification, to determine and report whether HKETOs merit privileges under 22 U.S.C. 288k. If not, HKETOs must end U.S. operations within 180 days and Congress may bar continuance via expedited joint resolution.

impact.summary: Bill requires Secretary of State, in each U.S.‑Hong Kong Policy Act certification, to report whether HKETOs merit U.S. privileges, exemptions, and immunities. If Secretary finds they do not merit benefits, HKETOs must cease U.S. operations within 180 days; Congress may enact a joint disapproval.

119/s/3655.title: Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office (HKETO) Certification Act

description.summary: The One Fair Price Act makes it unlawful to use surveillance data to offer or charge different prices for the same or substantially similar product or service. It authorizes FTC, State, and private enforcement with at least $3,000 damages, allows disclosed cost‑based differences and bona fide discounts/loyalty, and exempts insurance/credit.

impact.summary: The bill bars using surveillance data to set individualized prices for the same or substantially similar products or services, excluding insurance and credit. Enforcement would be by the Federal Trade Commission, state attorneys general, and private lawsuits with damages, covering retailers, online platforms, airlines.

description.summary: The bill directs OMB to consider adding a separate SOC code for direct support professionals as a healthcare support occupation in the next SOC revision. It covers workers who provide daily supports for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities and requires a congressional report if OMB declines.

impact.summary: The bill asks the OMB Director to consider adding a separate Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) code for direct support professionals. This would affect OMB and federal statistical agencies (including the BLS), States and home‑and‑community‑based service providers, and individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities.

119/s/3211.title: Recognizing the Role of Direct Support Professionals Act

description.summary: The bill creates a "catastrophic specialty hospital" designation that exempts qualifying LTCHs from the Medicare 1886(m) payment system. Applies to LTCHs with a 3-year track record of ≥80% spinal-cord or acquired-brain-injury DRG cases, ≥175 annual SCI and ABI discharges, ≥30% out‑of‑state admits, plus inpatient/outpatient services and neurorehab research/training.

impact.summary: The bill lets the HHS Secretary label some long term care hospitals as catastrophic specialty hospitals that mainly treat spinal cord or brain injuries. Those designated LTCHs would get Medicare payments outside the LTCH payment system, affecting LTCH operators and Medicare beneficiaries with those conditions.

description.summary: The Act directs the Energy Secretary to establish an Advanced AI Evaluation Program requiring developers of advanced AI (>10^26 ops) to provide code, training data, and model weights for government testing. It applies to developers supplying advanced AI for interstate or foreign commerce, prohibits deployment unless compliant, and imposes $1,000,000/day fines.

impact.summary: The bill requires the Secretary of Energy to establish the Advanced Artificial Intelligence Evaluation Program and compel covered developers to share models, code, and training data. It would affect major AI firms (OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Anthropic, Microsoft, Meta) and bar deployment without program compliance.

119/s/2938.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025

description.summary: This Senate resolution honors Kansas City, Kansas police officer Hunter Simoncic and memorializes his August 26, 2025 death while attempting to disable a fleeing vehicle, urging government support for his family. It is a nonbinding Senate expression covering Officer Simoncic, his family, and his legacy.

impact.summary: The Senate honors Kansas City, Kansas Officer Hunter Simoncic, killed August 26, 2025 on duty, and offers condolences to family. It pays tribute to his service with the Kansas City, Kansas Police Department and urges federal, Kansas state, and local governments to support his family.

119/sres/372.title: A resolution honoring the life of Kansas City, Kansas police officer Hunter Simoncic.

description.summary: S. Res. 425 is a Senate resolution honoring Hays, Kansas police Sergeant Scott Heimann, who was killed in the line of duty on September 27, 2025. It offers appreciation and condolences, pays tribute to his sacrifice, and urges government support for his family and Hays, Kansas.

impact.summary: The Senate honored Hays, Kansas Police Sergeant Scott Heimann and offered condolences to his wife Beth, Patrick, Victoria, parents Bill and Teresa Heimann. It pays tribute to his line-of-duty death and calls on federal, Kansas, and local governments to support his family.

119/sres/425.title: A resolution honoring the life of Hays, Kansas police sergeant Scott Heimann.

description.summary: The bill bars DOE from providing federal aid to state‑regulated investor‑owned electric utilities that raise residential rates above January 1, 2026 levels for one year. It permits aid after that only if utilities cap and cut total pay for their five top earners, report amounts, and forfeit aid for violations.

impact.summary: The bill bars the Secretary of Energy from aiding state regulated investor owned utilities for one year if they charge residential rates above January 1 2026 levels. After that, two-year aid requires cuts to total compensation for the five highest compensated employees and a report.

description.summary: The ELEVATE Act lets issuers submit draft registration statements to the SEC for confidential staff review before public filing and bars compelled disclosure of those submissions, treating them as confidential under FOIA exemptions and Exchange Act confidentiality rules. It also limits emerging growth companies to two years of financials.

impact.summary: The ELEVATE Act allows issuers to submit draft registration statements to the SEC for confidential review and requires public filing 10 days before listing. Emerging growth companies may report two prior fiscal years and confidential submissions are exempt from FOIA and protected under section 24.

description.summary: The bill directs NASA to designate national high‑energy astrophysics hubs to support X‑ray flagship missions, workforce development, mission planning and operations, scientific software, and tech transfer. Eligible hubs are NASA contractors that are universities, suitable state or federal entities (including FFRDCs), or NGOs with advanced energy research or commercialization expertise.

impact.summary: The bill directs NASA to designate national high energy astrophysics hubs to support X ray flagship missions and sustain US leadership. They would apply to NASA contractors, universities, FFRDCs, and NGOs, and to aerospace, spacecraft operations, and scientific software workforces and commercial partners.

119/s/4044.title: Support for Astrophysical Observatories and National High-Energy Astrophysics Hubs Act of 2026

description.summary: The Open Books, Open Doors Act creates a competitive Department of Education grant program to fund literacy materials, evidence-based programs, and family-literacy services. Grants prioritize projects serving "book deserts" and may be awarded to states, tribes, schools, libraries, juvenile-justice facilities, nonprofits, and community partners serving infants through young adults.

impact.summary: The Secretary of Education would award competitive grants to qualified applicants to provide books, evidence based literacy programs. Grants target "book deserts" and fund State and Tribal governments, SEAs, public libraries, schools, juvenile justice facilities, Head Start, WIC, barbershops, laundromats, bookstores, and community health centers.

description.summary: This bill bars the Secretary of State from charging a fee to issue or reissue U.S. passport cards, but permits fees for expedited processing. It applies to all passport card applicants and overrides the Passport Act of 1920's fee authority except for expedited-service charges.

impact.summary: The bill bars the Secretary of State and Department of State from charging fees for issuing or reissuing passport cards. It would affect U.S. citizens applying for passport cards and the Department's consular and passport offices that process them; expedited processing fees remain allowed.

description.summary: The Contract Our Veterans Act of 2026 amends the Small Business Act to establish a governmentwide 5% prime/subcontract goal and authorize sole-source and veteran-only restricted competitions for small business concerns owned and controlled by veterans. It adds veterans-owned provisions to federal contracting, SBA reporting, scorecards, mentor-protege rules, and subcontracting limits.

impact.summary: The bill requires the Small Business Administration and federal contracting officers to set a 5% goal for veteran‑owned small business awards. It permits restricted set‑asides and limited sole‑source awards and amends SBA reporting, scorecards, OSDBU duties, and subcontracting rules, affecting federal agencies and prime contractors.

description.summary: The bill authorizes the VA to recoup awards, bonuses, and relocation costs from former employees if a Director upholds a repayment order and repayment is unpaid after 180 days. It amends 38 U.S.C. §§721 and 723 to permit recovery as other federal debts and disallows waiver under 38 U.S.C. 5302.

impact.summary: The bill lets the Secretary of Veterans Affairs recoup awards, bonuses, and relocation expenses from former Department of Veterans Affairs employees who do not repay within 180 days after a Director upholds an order. Recovery uses federal debt-collection tools and cannot be waived.

119/hr/7319.title: VA Bonus and Relocation Recovery Act

description.summary: This bill lets the Director of the National Museum of African American History and Culture use federal funds to create and share African American history education resources, programs, and exhibitions. It funds teacher training, curricula, translations, online materials, collection digitization, and authorizes $4,000,000 annually for FY2027–FY2031.

impact.summary: The bill lets the Director of the National Museum of African American History and Culture use $4,000,000 yearly to fund curricula, digital resources, teacher training, exhibitions, and digitize collections. It would affect NMAAHC staff, Smithsonian museums, teachers, local educational agencies, K–12 schools, students, and families.

description.summary: The PAPERS Act requires DHS to return covered documents to individuals on release from custody, except when document is fraudulent, contraband or evidence in a pending criminal case, or not legally possessed. It covers passports, green cards, employment authorization documents, birth certificates, driver's licenses, Social Security cards, and similar papers.

impact.summary: The PAPERS Act would require the Secretary of Homeland Security to return government IDs to people released from DHS immigration custody. DHS may keep documents only for fraud, contraband/evidence, or no legal entitlement, and must give a written explanation plus a certified copy.

description.summary: This House resolution celebrates the YMCA's 175th anniversary and formally congratulates and recognizes its historical contributions to education, recreation, childcare, public health, and wartime humanitarian work. It commends YMCA staff and volunteers, encourages support to address social isolation, and notes roughly 2,600 locations serving communities in every State and territory.

impact.summary: This House resolution congratulates the Young Men's Christian Association (YMCA) on its 175th anniversary and recognizes its Chicago headquarters and ~2,600 locations nationwide. It honors YMCA staff and volunteers and spotlights programs — childcare, camps, swim lessons, and youth sports — that serve communities in every State.

119/hres/1074.title: Celebrating the 175th anniversary of the Young Men's Christian Association (YMCA).

description.summary: The bill expands VA caregiver benefits by extending 180‑day post‑program medical care, adding bereavement counseling, retirement planning and studies, and requiring employment assistance including training and a $1,000 certification reimbursement. It covers primary caregivers under 38 U.S.C. 1720G, excluding those dismissed for fraud, abuse, mistreatment, or entitled to Medicare.

impact.summary: The bill expands VA support for primary family caregivers, adding 180 days of medical coverage, bereavement counseling, retirement planning, and licensure reimbursement. It directs VA to study return-to-work programs and VA hiring and partner with Labor, Defense (Military OneSource), VETS, GAO, and Treasury.

119/hr/2148.title: Veteran Caregiver Reeducation, Reemployment, and Retirement Act

description.summary: Directs the GAO to study and report within 18 months how Federal reductions in force affect State and local budgets, revenues, services, and regional economies. It covers RIFs under title 5 and other significant federal civilian downsizings, and effects on States, the District of Columbia, territories, possessions, and local governments.

impact.summary: The bill directs the GAO to study how Federal RIFs affect State and local budgets, including unemployment insurance, Medicaid, retraining, housing, and tax revenues. GAO will consult OPM, the Department of Labor, state budget officers and governors, and report findings to House and Senate committees.

119/hr/7507.title: Fiscal Harms of Federal Firings Act

description.summary: The TRUST Act of 2026 raises the 10(d) asset threshold from $3,000,000,000 to $6,000,000,000, allowing Federal banking agencies to examine qualifying insured depository institutions no less than once every 18 months. It applies to qualifying insured depository institutions supervised by the FDIC, OCC, or Federal Reserve below $6 billion.

impact.summary: The bill raises the FDIA asset cutoff from $3B to $6B, letting federal banking agencies examine qualifying insured depository institutions every 18 months instead of more often. It affects FDIC‑insured banks and savings associations and the supervisors FDIC, OCC, and the Federal Reserve.

description.summary: This bill names the United States Postal Service facility at 15422 NY 104 in Martville, New York, the "Sergeant Staret J. Engleston Memorial Post Office Building." Federal laws, maps, regulations, and other official records referencing the facility will be deemed to use the new name.

impact.summary: The bill names the USPS facility at 15422 NY‑104 in Martville, New York, the "Sergeant Staret J. Engleston Memorial Post Office Building." It requires the Postal Service and federal laws, maps, and documents to use that name and affects local postal employees and customers.

119/hr/7410.title: To designate the facility of the United States Postal Service located at 15422 NY 104 in Martville, New York, as the "Sergeant Staret J. Engleston Memorial Post Office Building".

description.summary: The Save for Success Act lets Section 529 plan distributions pay a designated beneficiary’s qualified housing expenses for buying a principal residence, including closing and mortgage costs. It’s limited to first-time homebuyers (no ownership in prior three years, includes spouse) and applies to distributions after December 31, 2026.

impact.summary: The Save for Success Act would change the Internal Revenue Code to allow distributions from state-sponsored 529 qualified tuition programs for a beneficiary’s first‑time home purchase, including closing costs and mortgage payments. It would affect beneficiaries, savers, state 529 administrators, the IRS and mortgage lenders.

description.summary: The bill requires unspent agency appropriations be split: 49% held one more year, 49% for public-debt principal and interest, and 2% for retention bonuses (capped at 10% of basic pay), with leftovers to debt and next-year budgets tied to CPI. Coverage: executive agencies, US Postal Service, PRC; Red Cross excluded.

impact.summary: The bill makes Executive agencies (including USPS and PRC) split unspent funds: 49% kept one year, 49% for public debt, 2% for retention bonuses capped at 10% of basic pay. They must cap next-year budget requests to the prior request adjusted by CPI to OMB.

description.summary: This House resolution calls for portable health and retirement benefits, transparent revenue-sharing, algorithm and AI transparency, creator control of audience contacts, customer appeal rights, small‑business support, and protections against worker misclassification. It addresses creators, freelancers, and digital workers who earn income through online platforms and the platforms that host content.

impact.summary: The resolution supports portable benefits, timely appeals, small-business resources, and clear revenue-sharing and algorithmic transparency for creators and digital workers on platforms like YouTube, TikTok, Patreon, Substack, Uber, and DoorDash. It signals Congressional support to agencies like the Department of Labor, SBA, and FTC.

119/hres/1005.title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that creators and digital workers, as a distinct and growing class of small businesses and independent economic contributors, deserve fair treatment, transparency, and economic opportunity in the modern platform-based economy.

description.summary: The No Aid for Russian Energy Act bars U.S. persons and entities they own or control from providing petroleum equipment or services to persons in the Russian Federation. It covers equipment, software, cloud and consulting for oil and gas and authorizes asset-blocking, visa bans, penalties, narrow humanitarian and medical-isotope exceptions.

impact.summary: The bill bars U.S. persons and U.S.-owned foreign subsidiaries from providing petroleum equipment, software, cloud services, engineering, or training to persons in the Russian Federation. It authorizes Treasury/OFAC asset-blocking and State/DHS visa bans, creates penalties and presidential waivers, and exempts medical isotope and humanitarian supplies.

119/hr/7094.title: No Aid for Russian Energy Act

description.summary: The bill lets estates and donors deduct transfers to nonprofit cemetery companies and cemetery corporations chartered for burial, and makes private foundation payments to them count as qualifying distributions, not taxable expenditures. It applies to estate and gift tax years beginning after enactment and to foundation distributions made after enactment.

impact.summary: The bill lets estates and donors deduct federal estate and gift transfers to nonprofit cemetery companies or burial-only cemetery corporations. It also treats private foundation payments to those nonprofit cemeteries as meeting minimum distribution rules and not taxable expenditures under sections 4942 and 4945.

description.summary: This bill amends IRC section 121 to remove the $250,000 and $500,000 dollar limits on excluding gain from the sale of a principal residence. It applies to qualifying owners who meet the ownership and use tests for sales and exchanges after enactment.

impact.summary: The bill would change Internal Revenue Code section 121 to remove dollar limits on excluding gain from sales of principal residences. It would affect homeowners who sell their main homes, the IRS and Treasury revenues, and the residential real estate industry.

119/hr/7034.title: To amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to eliminate the dollar limitations on the exclusion of gain from sales of principal residences, and for other purposes.

description.summary: The bill forbids using federal funds for military force in or against Venezuela until December 31, 2026, unless Congress declares war or enacts a WPR compliant authorization. It applies to all funds appropriated or otherwise made available to the Federal Government and excludes uses consistent with War Powers Resolution section 2(c).

impact.summary: The bill bars federal funds from being used for U.S. military force in or against Venezuela through December 31, 2026, unless Congress declares war or enacts a War Powers authorization. It directly restricts the Department of Defense, U.S. Southern Command, the President, and defense contractors.

119/hr/6915.title: To prohibit the use of funds to use military force in or against Venezuela, and for other purposes.

description.summary: The RELIEVE Act waives the 24‑month VA‑care prerequisite for reimbursement of emergency treatment provided within 60 days after a veteran enrolls. It amends 38 U.S.C. 1725(b)(2)(B), takes effect for care furnished one year after enactment, and covers veterans seeking emergency care through the Veterans Community Care program.

impact.summary: RELIEVE lets the VA reimburse non‑VA providers for emergency care within 60 days after a veteran enrolls in VA health care. It affects veterans enrolling in VA care, the VA’s Veterans Community Care program, and non‑VA providers, applying to care furnished one year after enactment.

description.summary: The bill adds four areas in the Angeles National Forest to the National Wilderness Preservation System: Condor Peak, San Gabriel, Sheep Mountain, and Yerba Buena. It applies to federal lands in the Angeles National Forest, withdraws them from mineral entry, and directs the Secretary to manage fire, wildlife, and recreation.

impact.summary: The bill makes four new wilderness units in the Angeles National Forest—Condor Peak, San Gabriel additions, Sheep Mountain additions, and Yerba Buena—and withdraws them from mining and mineral leasing. The U.S. Forest Service will administer them and update fire plans with State and local agencies.

119/hr/6783.title: San Gabriel Mountains, Foothills, and Rivers Protection Act of 2025

description.summary: The ARMAS Act of 2025 transfers export licensing and regulatory control of certain firearms and munitions from Commerce to State. It covers U.S. exports tied to trafficking into Mexico, Central America, and the Caribbean and mandates reports, tracing expansion, changes to Caribbean security assistance, license limits, and promotion bans.

impact.summary: ARMAS would move export control of U.S. firearms and munitions from Commerce to State. It would add certification and licensing limits, require reports and strategies to curb trafficking to Mexico and Central American and Caribbean countries, and expand eTrace and Caribbean Basin Security Initiative support.

description.summary: This bill exempts certain less-than-lethal projectile devices and ammunition from the federal firearms/ammunition excise tax and from NFA coverage. It defines covered devices by technical limits (nonconvertible to common firearm ammo, no semiauto feeding, projectiles ≤500 ft/s), requires IRS classification, annual lists and a report, and applies to post‑enactment sales.

impact.summary: The bill exempts certain less-than-lethal projectile devices and related cartridges from the federal firearms and ammunition excise tax and from National Firearms Act (NFA) classification, affecting manufacturers and importers of those devices. The Treasury Secretary must make 90‑day rulings, publish annual device lists, and report to House Ways and Means and Senate Finance.

description.summary: The bill authorizes duty‑free preferential treatment for imports from qualifying Pacific Islands countries and directs the President to designate eligible countries using AGOA/Trade Act criteria. It applies to imports entering the U.S., waives income thresholds, excludes countries for worker, human‑rights, or environmental failures, and requires an FTA plan and report.

impact.summary: The PROSPER Act authorizes the President to grant preferential tariffs on goods from Pacific Islands, affecting Pacific exporters and U.S. importers. It conditions eligibility on Trade Act and AGOA labor, human rights, and environmental standards and directs USTR and Congress consultations on free trade plans.

description.summary: The bill exempts actions by the Advocate for Small Business Capital Formation from being a "collection of information" under the Paperwork Reduction Act. It amends Section 4(i) of the Securities Exchange Act, preserves some PRA review duties, but exempts the SEC from OMB submission, control-number display, and clearance labeling.

impact.summary: The bill exempts the SEC's Advocate for Small Business Capital Formation from being a "collection of information" under the Paperwork Reduction Act. It removes OMB submission and control-number requirements and affects the SEC, OMB, small issuers, startups, and others who work with the Advocate.

119/s/3411.title: Improving Access to Small Business Information Act

description.summary: The DO NOT Call Act adds criminal penalties to 47 U.S.C. 227 for willful, knowing TCPA violations—up to 1 year imprisonment, or up to 3 years for aggravated offenses—and raises caller ID falsification fines to $20,000. It covers autodialed or prerecorded voice calls and texts to NANP numbers, including emergencies.

impact.summary: The bill adds federal criminal penalties to the Telephone Consumer Protection Act, allowing up to one year imprisonment or three years for aggravated robocallers. It raises caller‑ID fines to $20,000 and authorizes DOJ prosecutions alongside FCC enforcement, affecting telemarketers, debt collectors, phone carriers, and consumers.

description.summary: The HALOS Act directs the SEC to amend Regulation D within six months so issuer presentations at qualifying sponsored events are not deemed general solicitation. It applies to non‑bankrupt business issuers (not investment companies or shell/blank‑check firms) presenting at specified sponsored events, subject to sponsor conduct and disclosure limits.

impact.summary: The bill directs the Securities and Exchange Commission to amend Regulation D to allow issuer presentations at sponsored events despite the general solicitation ban. It affects issuers (early‑stage companies), the SEC, angel investor groups of accredited investors, incubators, colleges, states, tribes, nonprofits, and event sponsors.

description.summary: The bill amends INA section 329A to grant posthumous U.S. citizenship to otherwise qualified noncitizens who enlisted in the Philippines and died on active duty with U.S. Armed Forces between September 1, 1939 and December 31, 1946. The executive department must certify eligibility and certain timing and benefit limits waived.

impact.summary: The bill amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to grant honorary posthumous U.S. citizenship to noncitizens who enlisted in the Philippines and died on active duty in the U.S. Armed Forces between September 1, 1939, and December 31, 1946. It directs military departments to certify.

119/hr/6355.title: Corporal Fernando Ruiz Baltazar Posthumous Citizenship Act of 2025

description.summary: Wildfire Recovery Act makes FMAG federal share at least 75% and requires FEMA to adopt rules within three years setting criteria, including a financial-impact threshold, to recommend raising that share. It applies to FMAG funds appropriated after enactment and makes State, local, and Tribal predeployment costs reimbursable.

impact.summary: The bill makes FEMA FMAG federal share at least 75% and requires rulemaking so the Administrator may recommend to the President raising that share when a financial threshold is met. It allows reimbursement of predeployment costs for State, local, and Tribal firefighting assets.

description.summary: CREATIVE establishes a competitive federal grant program funding hiring (up to $5,000,000) and construction/maintenance (up to $3,000,000) for arts productions, facilities, and programming. Grants fund eligible arts entities to employ professional performers and related staff, prioritize underserved communities, require community outreach and labor protections, and limit recipients to one grant.

impact.summary: The CREATIVE Act creates a Commerce-run grant program for arts jobs. The Economic Development Administration would award competitive grants (up to $5 million for hiring, $3 million for construction/maintenance) to arts nonprofits, theaters, and museums to hire performers, writers, and related staff with NEA labor-standards.

description.summary: The bill permits an emerging growth company to omit acquired‑company financial statements for periods before the earliest audited period shown in its IPO. It amends Securities Act section 7(a)(2) and Exchange Act 12(b)(1)(K) filings and prohibits later requiring those pre‑IPO periods even after the issuer ceases to be an EGC.

impact.summary: The Greenlighting Growth Act lets emerging growth companies (EGCs) and former EGC issuers omit acquired‑company financial statements and 17 C.F.R. §210.3‑05/210.8‑04 disclosures for periods before their earliest audited IPO year. It affects SEC‑registered issuers, auditors, underwriters, and investors.

description.summary: The bill repeals the firearm-related provisions of the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act and restores affected federal statutes to their pre‑enactment texts. It removes related amendments to the federal criminal code, the Brady Act and education law and eliminates grant funding for states to add juvenile records to NICS.

impact.summary: The bill would repeal the firearm-related provisions of the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act and restore pre-enactment federal gun law language. It would affect the FBI NICS system, ATF, DOJ grants (OJP), state criminal records offices submitting juvenile records, and public schools under ESEA.

description.summary: The bill directs the Secretary of Transportation to allow States to offer online registration and renewal for seasonal farm-related service-industry restricted commercial driver's licenses. It also clarifies within one year that implements of husbandry are not commercial motor vehicles and are excluded from gross combination weight rating calculations.

impact.summary: DOT would let States offer online registration and renewal for seasonal restricted CDLs used by farm-related service industries and eligible employees. It clarifies implements of husbandry are not commercial motor vehicles and not subject to gross combination weight calculations, affecting farmers and State licensing.

description.summary: The bill adds "fusion energy components" to Internal Revenue Code section 45X, making them eligible for the advanced manufacturing production credit equal to 25% of a component's sales price and phasing that credit out between 2032–2034 to 0% thereafter. Scope: defined fusion parts and systems for machines producing electricity or process heat.

impact.summary: The bill makes many fusion components eligible for a 25% Section 45X advanced manufacturing tax credit. That affects U.S. fusion component manufacturers, fusion companies and suppliers, requires Treasury/IRS administration, and phases out from 2032 through 2034.

description.summary: The bill directs the Secretary of Labor to allow ERISA pension administrators to voluntarily transfer unclaimed retirement distributions to State unclaimed property programs through a national clearinghouse. It applies to ERISA plans' distributions $50 or more, requires locator searches and notice, 90‑day reporting to Labor, and provides ERISA fiduciary safe‑harbor.

impact.summary: The bill directs the Secretary of Labor to let pension plan administrators transfer unclaimed retirement funds to State unclaimed property programs. It requires searches, notice and reports to the Department of Labor and Retirement Savings Lost and Found, and grants ERISA and IRS protection.

description.summary: The bill extends TDAPA and TPNIES to at least three years and mandates a permanent post-TDAPA add-on for new renal dialysis drugs equal to 65% of utilization-based per-service costs. It covers FDA-approved products, devices, capital assets, Medicare ESRD enrollees, dialysis facilities, providers, and Medicare Advantage starting January 1, 2026.

impact.summary: The bill requires HHS/CMS to extend transitional add‑on payments and establish a permanent post‑TDAPA add‑on for FDA‑approved renal dialysis drugs and devices beginning January 1, 2026. It affects Medicare ESRD beneficiaries, renal dialysis facilities and providers, Medicare Advantage plans, and drug and device manufacturers.

description.summary: This House resolution expresses support for designating March 24, 2026, as "National Agriculture Day" and formally celebrates agriculture as one of the United States' most impactful industries. It is a nonbinding, symbolic statement by the House of Representatives recognizing agriculture nationwide and does not create legal rights, obligations, or funding.

impact.summary: This House resolution would express support for designating March 24, 2026, as "National Agriculture Day" and encourage recognition of that day. It would symbolically involve the U.S. Department of Agriculture, state departments of agriculture, farmers, ranchers, farmworkers, agribusinesses, land‑grant universities, FFA, 4‑H and agricultural communities.

119/hres/1132.title: Expressing support for the designation of March 24, 2026, as "National Agriculture Day" and celebrating the importance of agriculture as one of the most impactful industries in the United States.

description.summary: The bill excludes de minimis gains or losses from virtual currency sales or exchanges from gross income unless the transaction's value or gain/loss exceeds $200 or it is exchanged for cash or business/income‑producing property. It defines virtual currency as digital value (excluding U.S./foreign currency) and applies to transactions after 2026.

impact.summary: The bill excludes de minimis gains or losses from virtual currency sales or exchanges from gross income, affecting U.S. taxpayers, cryptocurrency exchanges, businesses accepting crypto, tax preparers, and the IRS. It applies to transactions $200 or less (aggregated) and takes effect after December 31, 2026.

description.summary: The bill raises Section 3(b)'s Regulation A exemption from $50 million to $150 million and requires the SEC to adjust it biennially for CPI‑U inflation to the nearest $10,000. It covers issuers using the Section 3(b)/Regulation A exemption for small‑company offerings and updates related paragraph references to incorporate the inflation adjustment.

impact.summary: The bill raises the Regulation A offering cap from $50 million to $150 million and requires the Securities and Exchange Commission to adjust it for CPI every two years to the nearest $10,000. It affects small companies and startups using Regulation A, their investors, and SEC oversight duties.

description.summary: This Senate resolution supports annually designating the first Saturday after the spring equinox as "National Day of Play" to encourage play and reduced device use. It urges individuals and community institutions—schools, workplaces, places of worship, parks, and neighborhood groups—nationwide to host device-reduced play events that promote social connection and health.

impact.summary: The Senate resolution names the first Saturday after the Spring Equinox as "National Day of Play." It encourages Americans, families, schools, parks and recreation departments, local governments, and the Surgeon General to promote device‑free, community play events.

119/sres/655.title: A resolution expressing support for the annual designation of the first Saturday after the Spring Equinox as "National Day of Play".

description.summary: This resolution designates the week beginning March 15, 2026, as "National CACFP Week" and recognizes the Child and Adult Care Food Program's provision of nutritious meals and snacks. It covers children and adults served by CACFP in centers, family day homes, shelters, adult day care, and after‑school programs nationwide.

impact.summary: The Senate designates the week beginning March 15, 2026, as National CACFP Week to recognize the USDA Child and Adult Care Food Program. It serves children and adults in child care centers, family day care homes, emergency shelters, after‑school programs, and adult day care facilities.

119/sres/656.title: A resolution designating the third week of March 2026 as "National CACFP Week".

description.summary: The Senate designated March 21, 2026, as National Women in Agriculture Day and urges citizens to recognize and support women in agricultural careers and leadership. It covers U.S. women in agriculture—over 1.2 million producers accounting for 41% of 2022 sales ($222 billion)—including educators, mentors, and agribusiness leaders.

impact.summary: The Senate designates March 21, 2026, as National Women in Agriculture Day recognizing women agricultural producers, farm operators, educators, researchers, and agribusiness. It encourages public to praise and support women via 4‑H, National FFA, Cooperative Extension, and agricultural education to boost leadership and workforce participation.

119/sres/653.title: A resolution designating March 21, 2026, as "National Women in Agriculture Day".

description.summary: The bill directs the Secretary of Agriculture, through NIFA, to study accessibility of addiction and mental health providers and services and identify barriers, best practices, and federal recommendations. It covers farmers, ranchers, agricultural workers, and their families affected by drought, extreme weather, commodity instability, misinformation, and related stressors.

119/hr/8149.title: Agricultural Access to Addiction and Mental Health Care Act

impact.summary: The bill requires USDA's Economic Research Service to publish after each Census a report on consolidation in beef, dairy, pork, and poultry. ERS must use NASS, FSIS, and AMS Packers and Stockyards data to analyze effects on ranchers, farmers, processing facilities, packers, and downstream consumers.

description.summary: The bill amends section 201(a) of the Civil Rights Act to deem an establishment that implements Sharia law in providing goods, services, facilities, privileges, advantages, or accommodations to be discriminating or segregating on the basis of religion. It covers establishments classed as public accommodations under section 201(a) nationwide.

impact.summary: The bill amends Section 201(a) of the Civil Rights Act to treat a covered public accommodation's use of "Sharia law" in providing goods or services as illegal religious discrimination. It would apply to hotels, restaurants, stores, hospitals, schools, mosques, Muslim-owned businesses, and DOJ enforcement.

119/hr/8017.title: Defeat Sharia Law in America Act

description.summary: The bill creates an NIJ task force to study use of AI speech‑to‑text and automatic speech recognition in U.S. courts. It requires a 15‑member panel (4 federal, 11 nonfederal) to assess feasibility, accuracy, privacy, and civil‑liberty issues and recommend reforms to safeguard constitutional rights and accurate court records.

119/s/4154.title: Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026

description.summary: The bill funds a pilot program awarding grants to States, Indian Tribes, and Tribal organizations to supplement wages of eligible child care workers. It covers center‑ and home‑based workers at licensed or registered providers nationwide including Tribal lands, with grants awarded based on child population, workforce size, wages, and subsidy gaps.

impact.summary: The Secretary of Health and Human Services would run a pilot awarding competitive grants to States, Indian Tribes, and Tribal organizations to supplement wages of eligible child care workers in licensed, regulated, or registered centers and family child care homes. It references CCDBG eligibility.
